vulnerability.title: Symfony DefaultAuthenticationFailureHandler honors the request-supplied _failure_path when failure_forward is enabled, allowing an unauthenticated firewall bypass via subrequest

vulnerability.category_l2: Firewall/access_control bypass through an attacker-controlled failure_forward subrequest target

critical_operation.description: onAuthenticationFailure() reads the _failure_path request parameter at line 74 and, when it starts with "/" or "http", writes it into $options['failure_path'] at line 77. Only afterwards, at line 84, does it test failure_forward; at line 89 that path becomes the target of an HttpUtils::createRequest() subrequest, which line 92 dispatches with HttpKernelInterface::SUB_REQUEST. Symfony's firewall skips subrequests and therefore does not run AccessListener, so an unauthenticated failing login can make the application execute any GET route outside the access_control perimeter and return its response. The 5.4.53 fix moves the failure_forward branch above the request-parameter handling, so forwarding uses only the application-configured failure_path (default login_path).

entry_point.description: An unauthenticated POST to the firewall check path on an application configured with form-login (or another authenticator using this handler) and failure_forward: true, with a _failure_path parameter naming a protected GET route.

required_before_promotion: An independent reviewer must read DefaultAuthenticationFailureHandler::onAuthenticationFailure at v5.4.45 and confirm the request parameter is assigned before the failure_forward branch.
An independent reviewer must confirm the subrequest target uses that value and is dispatched as SUB_REQUEST.
An independent reviewer must confirm c48a4276 is absent from v5.4.45 and present in v5.4.53, and that the fix only reorders the branches.
An independent reviewer must confirm the affected range includes 5.4.45 (and 5.4.52) and the fixed release is 5.4.53.
No formal reviews.jsonl row may be written until a named independent reviewer returns a verdict.

limitations: Single-reviewer dossier; not eligible for data/vulnerabilities.jsonl yet.
No Symfony application, firewall, HTTP request or subrequest was executed; the bypass is verified statically and was not reproduced.
The firewall/AccessListener subrequest-skipping behaviour is taken from the advisory text and was not re-read in the Firewall listener source.
Exploitation requires failure_forward: true and at least one GET route under a broad access_control rule.
Only the 5.4 branch was compared; 6.4.41, 7.4.13 and 8.0.13 were not diffed.
The snapshot v5.4.45 predates the 5.4.52 fixes, so this entry is independent of the other 2026 symfony CVEs.
open_questions: Whether other failure handlers or authenticators share the same ordering defect was not audited.
Whether the subrequest can reach routes that additionally depend on session state was not analysed.
